chunks: And from him, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

I heard him saying: ‘Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله slept, and his eyes overcame him, and he did not awaken until the heat of the sun harmed him. Then he awoke, and he returned his caller for a while, and performed two rakʿahs, then prayed the morning prayer, and said: “O Bilal, what is with you?” Bilal said: “The One who caused you to sleep caused me to sleep, O Messenger of Allah.” He said: and he disliked remaining there, and said: “You slept in the valley of Satan.”’

So the meaning in these two reports is that it is only permissible to perform two supererogatory rakʿahs so that the people who missed the prayer may gather and pray in congregation, just as the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله did. But if a person is alone, then it is not permissible for him to begin with any supererogatory prayer at all, according to what we have already stated; and what he narrated further clarifies it:

key_terms.رَسُولَ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, whose action is being cited as proof
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two units of prayer performed before the morning prayer in this report
key_terms.وَادِي الشَّيْطَانِ: the valley of Satan, the place in which they had slept

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform supererogatory prayer before making up the missed morning prayer?
ai.summary: This report recounts that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله missed the morning prayer due to sleep, then performed two rakʿahs before praying salat al-subh. The accompanying legal explanation states that these two rakʿahs are understood as being allowed for the purpose of gathering people for congregational prayer, not as a general permission for one praying alone to begin with supererogatory prayer after missing the obligatory prayer.
